calls.head: Strength vs. Strength
calls.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Senators are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Penguins’ chance quality wins out.

calls.head: Bruisers vs. Finesse
calls.body: On physicality, Ottawa is one of the league’s best, but Pittsburgh is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Senators.

surprises.head: Ottawa shut down Pittsburgh’s power play
surprises.body: Pittsburgh’s power play created 1.5 expected goals per 60, against their usual 6.7 (about 6.4 against Ottawa) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Amadio has a goal and an assist as the Senators beat the Penguins
paras: The first goal of the game would have been Pittsburgh’s, but it was taken off for offside early in the first. They got it back with just eight seconds left in the period, when Tommy Novak officially opened the scoring. Michael Amadio tied it up for Ottawa midway through the second, and Claude Giroux gave the Senators the lead late in the period. Tim Stützle extended the lead to 3-1 with less than six minutes left. Thomas Chabot added an empty-net goal with 32 seconds left to make it 4-1.

The Senators had the better of the chances, outshooting the Penguins 34-17. Linus Ullmark needed only 16 saves for the Sens, and Sergei Murashov stopped 30 of 33 at the other end. The Senators improved to 13-6-2 and climbed to third in the Atlantic, while the Penguins dropped to 7-11-2, slipping to seventh in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Tim Stützle passed Drake Batherson for eighth on the Senators’ all-time goals list, with 160.
The Senators have points in five straight games (4-0-1).
Philip Tomasino played his first game back in Pittsburgh.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
